analysis: The only change in this file is test-only: new expectations at head lines ~1257-1262 for a U.oneBuild(pinned:current:) helper in the onboarding-update logic (both Macs must report the same new build before a re-plan). The supplied units are base text, lines 1-867, and do not include the changed hunk or the implementation of oneBuild. The base text I reviewed is a model-free test harness using pseudo-terminals and scripted operations. It contains no production code, no key material, no network access and no authorization logic, and it touches no assets from the threat model, including the T-041 cache details. I did not see how oneBuild is implemented or used in production code. Whether it gates re-planning safely, for example by rejecting spoofed or missing build identifiers from a member, is outside the supplied evidence and is a question for review of the non-test source. The tests assert conservative behavior: wait when the other Mac has not answered, runs the old build, or was not asked, and do nothing with no setup. These expectations fit a fail-safe design. I found no security regression in the test file itself. Remaining integration question: confirm that the production implementation of ClusterOnboardingUpdate.oneBuild matches these expectations. In particular, it should require non-nil, equal build identifiers from both Macs that differ from the pinned build, and that identity should come from authenticated cluster-link responses.
